drivingQuestion: What distinguishes a day with musaf from a day with a wood offering?

segments.he: כׇּל יוֹם שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ הַלֵּל אֵין בּוֹ מַעֲמָד כּוּ׳. מָה הֶפְרֵשׁ בֵּין זֶה לָזֶה? הַלָּלוּ דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, וְהַלָּלוּ דִּבְרֵי סוֹפְרִים.
segments.en: The mishna taught: On «any day that has» the recitation of «hallel,» but on which the additional offering was not sacrificed, «it has no» reading of the Torah by the «non-priestly watch» in the morning service. On days that have both hallel and an additional offering, there was no reading in the afternoon prayer. When a wood offering was brought, there was no reading in the closing prayer. The Gemara asks: «What is» the «difference between this and that,» a day on which an additional offering is sacrificed and a day on which a wood offering is brought? The Gemara explains: «These» days, on which an additional offering is brought, apply «by Torah law, but these» days, on which a wood offering is brought, apply «by rabbinic law,» and therefore it overrides only the closing prayer.
